page.layout: One page of text in a single column; in the right margin, notes beside the lines of the lower part (marked II., Pelagiana & Semipelagiana, and the catchword-area mark B at the foot). Page number at the head centre.

main_text.l: voluntas Dei est prima causa omniū: (
Facit enim Deus omnia, de consilio voluntatis
suæ. Eph. 1. v. 11.) quid absurdi est, sta-
tuere, quòd divina voluntas prius vult res
esse, quàm suus intellectus judicet, res fore. Ne-
que enim ideò vult Deus, quia prævi-
dit futuras, sive velit, sive nolit: ( nihil
enim futurum est, nisi ipsius voluntate
prægressâ, ut causâ futurorum ) sed,
quia vult, futuræ sunt.
Atque ita hæc Scylla, quæ putatur, & re-
vera non est, declinata est: ideoque nihil
hîc metuendum periculi, ubi omnia ( uti
partim jam vidimus; partim amplius vi-
dere est apud nostros doctores, & ipsū
etiam Augustinum, Prosperum, alios-
que Patres ) planissimis Scripturæ
dictis constant.
Ex altera verò parte, non solùm peri-
culosa est illa Charybdis, in Pelagianismo &
Semipelagianismo, quæ refertur verbis s-
ynodi Arausicanæ secundæ ( Nullam
esse humanæ naturæ depravationem: Grati-
am ad solā remissione peccatorum valere,
&c.) damnata Synodis compluribus, quarum nūm
B

page.notes: Right-margin notes read "II." and "Pelagiana & Semipelagiana"; the mark at the foot is a signature-type letter "B" and is given as a foot line. Line ends "nūm" at the foot of the page is cut off by the page edge and may continue on the next page. Lines of the first paragraph with the word "quod" appear as "quòd"; the scan is slightly blurred in the lower third, so the reading of "Synodis compluribus" and "Scripturae dictis" is uncertain. Several words in the Scylla sentence (e.g. "putatur", "declinata") are only moderately clear.
